source.text: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·

records.literal_gloss: In the day that having gone out the Jesus from the house was sitting beside the sea;

en.L: On that day Jesus went out of the house and was sitting beside the sea;
en.B: That same day Jesus left the house and sat down beside the lake.
en.R: That same day Jesus left the house where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was staying. He went and sat down by Lake Galilee.

es.L: En aquel día, habiendo salido Jesús de la casa, estaba sentado a la orilla del mar;
es.B: Ese mismo día Jesús salió de la casa y se sentó a orillas del lago.
es.R: Ese mismo día, Jesús salió de la casa donde se alojaba. Fue y se sentó a la orilla del lago de Galilea.

sw.L: Siku ile Yesu, akiwa ametoka nyumbani, alikuwa ameketi kando ya bahari;
sw.B: Siku hiyo hiyo Yesu alitoka nyumbani, akaenda kuketi kando ya ziwa.
sw.R: Siku hiyo hiyo Yesu alitoka katika nyumba aliyokuwa akikaa. Akaenda kuketi kando ya Ziwa Galilaya.

decisions.choice: on that day: the day of the events of chapter 12
decisions.reason: Matthew joins the parables to the conflict of chapter 12. The house is likely the one of 12:46, where his family stood outside, and Jesus goes out of it to teach the crowds.

decisions.choice: sitting beside the sea: on the shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: The Gospels call the lake a sea (4:18). Sitting was the posture of a teacher (5:1).

decisions.choice: the lake (B); Lake Galilee (R); the sea (L)
decisions.reason: As at 8:24, Balanced and Readable call it a lake, which is what it is.

decisions.choice: the house where he was staying
decisions.reason: Readable says why there was a house to leave. Matthew does not say whose house it was.

decisions.choice: el mar (L); el lago (B); el lago de Galilea (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the "sea" is the Sea of Galilee, a freshwater lake (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "mar", the word of the Greek.

decisions.choice: bahari (L); ziwa (B); Ziwa Galilaya (R)
decisions.reason: Swahili "bahari" is the open sea; the Sea of Galilee is a freshwater lake (meaning decision m2), which Swahili calls "ziwa", as in Ziwa Viktoria. Literal keeps "bahari", the word of the Greek.

source.text: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.

records.literal_gloss: And were gathered to him crowds great, so that him into a boat having embarked to sit, and all the crowd on the shore was standing.

en.L: And large crowds gathered to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat down, and the whole crowd was standing on the shore.
en.B: Such great crowds gathered around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat down in it, while all the people stood on the shore.
en.R: So many people came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got into a boat and sat down in it. All the people stood on the shore.

es.L: Y se reunieron junto a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} grandes multitudes, de modo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, subiendo a una barca, se sentó, y toda la multitud estaba de pie en la orilla.
es.B: Se juntaron a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor multitudes tan grandes que subió a una barca y se sentó en ella, mientras toda la gente se quedaba de pie en la orilla.
es.R: Tanta gente se acercó a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} que subió a una barca y se sentó en ella. Toda la gente se quedó de pie en la orilla.

sw.L: Na makundi mengi ya watu yakakusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, hivi kwamba {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliingia katika mashua akaketi, na umati wote ulikuwa umesimama ufuoni.
sw.B: Makundi makubwa ya watu yalikusanyika {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, hata akaingia katika mashua na kuketi ndani yake, nao watu wote walisimama ufuoni.
sw.R: Watu wengi sana walikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, hata akaingia katika mashua, akaketi ndani yake. Watu wote walisimama ufuoni.

decisions.choice: sat in a boat: taught from a boat just off the shore
decisions.reason: A boat a little way out let the whole crowd see and hear him. Sitting was the posture of a teacher (5:1; 13:1).

decisions.choice: was standing: the crowd stood on the shore the whole time he taught
decisions.reason: The tense pictures the crowd standing as the teaching went on.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: él (L, R), su (B)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("subió a una barca"), so there is nothing separate to capitalise and the setting covers fewer words than in English. Literal keeps the second "él", since the Greek names him again. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans on kwake and yeye; none on the prefixes of akaingia, akaketi
decisions.reason: Swahili carries most pronouns in the verb prefix, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

source.text: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων· Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.

records.literal_gloss: And he spoke to them many things in parables saying, Behold, went out the sowing to sow.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke many things to them in parables, saying, "Look, the sower went out to sow.
en.B: He told them many things in parables. "Listen!" {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "A sower went out to sow.
en.R: He taught them many things by using parables. Parables are stories that teach a lesson. Jesus said, "Listen! A farmer went out to plant seed.

es.L: Y les habló de muchas cosas en parábolas, diciendo: «{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}: salió el sembrador a sembrar.
es.B: Les dijo muchas cosas en parábolas: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Un sembrador salió a sembrar.
es.R: Les enseñó muchas cosas por medio de parábolas. Las parábolas son historias que enseñan una lección. Jesús dijo: «¡{{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}}! Un agricultor salió a sembrar semillas.

sw.L: Naye alisema nao mambo mengi kwa mifano, akisema, "Angalieni, mpandaji alitoka ili apande.
sw.B: Aliwaeleza mambo mengi kwa mifano. Akasema, "Sikilizeni! Mpandaji mmoja alikwenda kupanda mbegu.
sw.R: Aliwafundisha mambo mengi kwa kutumia mifano. Mifano ni hadithi zinazofundisha somo. Yesu akasema, "Sikilizeni! Mkulima mmoja alikwenda shambani kupanda mbegu.

decisions.choice: parables: stories and word pictures from daily life that teach about God's kingdom
decisions.reason: The word means a comparison. It covers proverbs, riddles and stories. These parables compare the kingdom of heaven to what happens on a farm, in a kitchen and at sea, and they need explaining (13:10-18, 36).

decisions.choice: the sower: a typical sower, the one in the story
alternatives: a particular man the crowd knew
decisions.reason: The article points to the figure of the story, as is usual in parables.

decisions.choice: sowing: scattering seed by hand over a field
decisions.reason: The farmer threw seed by hand as he walked, so some fell on the path and on poor ground at the edges.

decisions.choice: look (L); listen (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: Parables are stories that teach a lesson
decisions.reason: This is the first time Matthew uses the word. Readable keeps "parables" and says what they are.

decisions.choice: the sower (L); a sower (B); a farmer (R); no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: Readable names a farmer, the person who did the sowing. The sower is a figure in a parable, so the pronouns for him take no deity_pronoun span, as with the bridegroom at 9:15. Jesus later says who sows the good seed (13:37).

decisions.choice: parábola (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet word for the Gospels, recorded once in this passage. It is the word Spanish readers know for these stories (meaning decision m1); Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} (L); {{plural_you:Escuchen|Escuchad}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the crowd, so the command is plural and takes the ustedes / vosotros setting, which has no English counterpart. The same for every plural "you" in this passage, to the crowd and then to the disciples.

decisions.choice: mfano (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet word for the Gospels, recorded once in this passage. "Mfano" is a comparison or picture-story, the usual word for these stories (meaning decision m1); "fumbo" is a riddle. Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: And in the sowing of him some indeed fell beside the road, and having come the birds devoured them.

en.L: And as he sowed, some [seeds] fell beside the road, and the birds came and devoured them.
en.B: As he was sowing, some of the seed landed beside the path, and the birds came and ate it all up.
en.R: As he threw the seed, some of it landed on the path. Birds came and ate it.

es.L: Y mientras él sembraba, unas [semillas] cayeron junto al camino, y llegaron las aves y las devoraron.
es.B: Mientras sembraba, parte de la semilla cayó al borde del sendero, y llegaron los pájaros y se la comieron toda.
es.R: Mientras echaba la semilla, una parte cayó en el camino. Vinieron unos pájaros y se la comieron.

sw.L: Na katika kupanda kwake, [mbegu] nyingine zilianguka kando ya njia, na ndege walipokuja walizimeza.
sw.B: Alipokuwa akipanda, baadhi ya mbegu zilianguka kando ya njia, nao ndege wakaja wakazidonoa zote.
sw.R: Alipokuwa akirusha mbegu, nyingine zilianguka juu ya njia. Ndege walikuja wakazila.

decisions.choice: beside the road: on or along the hard path through or around the field
decisions.reason: Paths ran along and through the fields. Seed that fell there lay on hard ground, where birds found it at once.

decisions.choice: some: some seeds (the word is plural)
decisions.reason: The plural refers to seeds, which the story does not name.

decisions.choice: the path (B, R); the road (L)
decisions.reason: The word means a way or road. In a field it is a footpath.

source.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς, ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.

records.literal_gloss: Others but fell upon the rocky places where not it had soil much, and immediately sprang up because of the not having depth of soil, \v 6 sun but having risen they were scorched and because of the not having root were dried up.

en.L: And others fell on the rocky places, where they did not have much soil, and at once they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil; \v 6 but when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they withered.
en.B: Some landed on rocky patches where the soil was thin. They shot up at once, since the soil was not deep, \v 6 but when the sun came up, the young plants were scorched, and having no root, they dried up.
en.R: Some seed landed on rocky ground, where there was not much soil. The plants came up quickly, because the soil was not deep. \v 6 But when the sun rose, the plants burned up in the heat. They dried up and died, because their roots did not go down deep.

es.L: Y otras cayeron sobre los terrenos pedregosos, donde no tenían mucha tierra, y al instante brotaron por no tener tierra honda; \v 6 pero al salir el sol quedaron abrasadas, y por no tener raíz se marchitaron.
es.B: Otra parte cayó en terreno pedregoso, donde la capa de tierra era delgada. Brotó enseguida, porque la tierra no era profunda, \v 6 pero cuando salió el sol, las plantas tiernas se quemaron y, como no tenían raíz, se secaron.
es.R: Otra parte de la semilla cayó en un terreno lleno de piedras, donde había poca tierra. Las plantas salieron pronto, porque la tierra no era profunda. \v 6 Pero cuando salió el sol, el calor las quemó. Se secaron y murieron, porque sus raíces no llegaban hondo.

sw.L: Na nyingine zilianguka juu ya mahali penye miamba, ambapo hapakuwa na udongo mwingi, na mara moja zikachipuka kwa sababu ya kutokuwa na kina cha udongo; \v 6 lakini jua lilipochomoza, ziliungua, na kwa sababu ya kutokuwa na mizizi, zikanyauka.
sw.B: Nyingine zilianguka kwenye sehemu zenye miamba ambapo udongo ulikuwa kidogo. Zilichipuka upesi kwa kuwa udongo haukuwa na kina, \v 6 lakini jua lilipochomoza, mimea hiyo michanga iliungua, na kwa kuwa haikuwa na mizizi, ikanyauka.
sw.R: Mbegu nyingine zilianguka kwenye ardhi yenye mawe mengi, ambapo udongo ulikuwa mchache. Mimea iliota haraka, kwa sababu udongo haukuwa na kina. \v 6 Lakini jua lilipochomoza, joto lake likaiunguza mimea hiyo. Ikakauka na kufa, kwa sababu mizizi yake haikwenda chini sana.

decisions.choice: rocky places: rock with only a thin layer of soil over it
decisions.reason: Much of Galilee has limestone close under the surface. The seed warms and sprouts fast, but the roots cannot go down.

decisions.choice: others ... they were scorched: the seeds, then the plants that grow from them
decisions.reason: The Greek goes on with "they" as the seeds become plants.

decisions.choice: burned up in the heat
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the sun did.

source.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἔπνιξαν αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: Others but fell upon the thorns, and came up the thorns and choked them.

en.L: And others fell on the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.
en.B: Other seed landed among thornbushes, and the thorns shot up and smothered it.
en.R: Some seed landed where thorny weeds were growing. The weeds grew up and crowded out the young plants.

es.L: Y otras cayeron sobre las espinas, y crecieron las espinas y las sofocaron.
es.B: Otra parte cayó entre zarzas, y las zarzas brotaron y la sofocaron.
es.R: Otra parte cayó donde crecían hierbas con espinas. Esas hierbas crecieron y les quitaron el espacio a las plantas nuevas.

sw.L: Na nyingine zilianguka kati ya miiba, na miiba ikapanda juu ikazikaba.
sw.B: Nyingine zilianguka kati ya vichaka vya miiba, nayo miiba ikakua ikazikaba.
sw.R: Mbegu nyingine zilianguka mahali palipokuwa na magugu yenye miiba. Magugu hayo yalikua, yakaibana mimea michanga isiweze kukua.

decisions.choice: thorns: thorny weeds whose roots were already in the ground
decisions.reason: The ground looked clear when the seed fell, but the thorns came up with the grain and took its light and water.

decisions.choice: crowded out the young plants
decisions.reason: Readable says how the thorns killed the grain.

source.text: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: Others but fell upon the soil the good and was giving fruit, some indeed a hundred, some but sixty, some but thirty.

en.L: And others fell on the good soil and were yielding fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
en.B: But other seed landed in good soil and went on to bear grain, a hundred times as much as was sown, or sixty, or thirty.
en.R: But some seed landed on good soil. It grew and made a big crop. Some plants made a hundred times as much grain as was planted. Some made sixty times as much, and some made thirty times as much.

es.L: Y otras cayeron sobre la tierra buena e iban dando fruto, unas cien [veces], otras sesenta, otras treinta.
es.B: Pero otra parte cayó en buena tierra y llegó a dar grano: cien veces más de lo sembrado, o sesenta, o treinta.
es.R: Pero otra parte cayó en tierra buena. Creció y dio una gran cosecha. Algunas plantas dieron cien veces más grano del que se había sembrado. Otras dieron sesenta veces más, y otras treinta veces más.

sw.L: Na nyingine zilianguka kwenye ardhi nzuri, zikaendelea kutoa mazao, nyingine [mara] mia, nyingine sitini, nyingine thelathini.
sw.B: Lakini nyingine zilianguka kwenye udongo mzuri, zikatoa nafaka: mara mia ya kile kilichopandwa, au mara sitini, au mara thelathini.
sw.R: Lakini mbegu nyingine zilianguka kwenye udongo mzuri. Zilikua, zikatoa mavuno mengi. Mimea mingine ilitoa nafaka mara mia ya mbegu zilizopandwa. Mingine ilitoa mara sitini, na mingine mara thelathini.

decisions.choice: a hundred, sixty, thirty: times as much as was sown
alternatives: a hundred, sixty or thirty plants
decisions.reason: The numbers count the yield. A good harvest was perhaps ten times the seed, so these are very large crops (compare Genesis 26:12, where Isaac reaps a hundredfold).

decisions.choice: fruit: grain, the crop
decisions.reason: The word is used of any crop. It prepares for the meaning given in 13:23.

decisions.choice: times as much as was sown (B); times as much grain as was planted (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the numbers count.

source.text: ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκουέτω.

records.literal_gloss: The one having ears let him hear.

en.L: The one who has ears, let him hear."
en.B: Whoever has ears must listen."
en.R: If you can hear {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, pay attention to this!"

es.L: El que tiene oídos, que oiga».
es.B: Quien tenga oídos, que escuche».
es.R: ¡Si {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}, {{plural_you:presten|prestad}} atención a esto!».

sw.L: Aliye na masikio, na asikie."
sw.B: Yeyote aliye na masikio na asikilize."
sw.R: Kama mnaweza kunisikia, yasikilizeni haya kwa makini!"

decisions.choice: whoever has ears, let him hear: a call to listen closely and take the saying to heart
decisions.reason: As at 11:15. The parable has a meaning the hearer must think about, as 13:10-17 shows.

decisions.choice: ears, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: ears to hear, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "ears to hear", as in Mark 4:9 and Luke 8:8. Some early manuscripts have only "ears". The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: If you can hear me, pay attention to this!
alternatives: The one who has ears, let him hear
decisions.reason: Readable gives the force of the saying in plain words, as at 11:15.

source.text: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;

records.literal_gloss: And having come the disciples said to him, Why in parables do you speak to them?

en.L: And the disciples came and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speak to them in parables?"
en.B: The disciples came up to Jesus and asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} using parables when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} talk to them?"
en.R: Then the followers of Jesus came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They asked, "Why do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} use parables when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} teach the people?"

es.L: Y acercándose los discípulos, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «¿Por qué les hablas en parábolas?».
es.B: Los discípulos se acercaron a Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué usas parábolas cuando les hablas?».
es.R: Entonces los discípulos de Jesús se acercaron a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} preguntaron: «¿Por qué usas parábolas cuando enseñas a la gente?».

sw.L: Na wanafunzi, wakiwa wamemkaribia, walimwambia, "Mbona kwa mifano unaongea nao?"
sw.B: Wanafunzi walimjia Yesu, wakamuuliza, "Kwa nini unatumia mifano unapozungumza nao?"
sw.R: Kisha wanafunzi wa Yesu walimjia, wakamuuliza, "Kwa nini unatumia mifano unapowafundisha watu?"

decisions.choice: to them: to the crowds
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke to the crowds from the boat (13:2-3). The disciples are set apart from them.

decisions.choice: came: came to him, perhaps later and away from the crowd
alternatives: while he was still in the boat
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say when they asked. Mark 4:10 says it was when Jesus was alone.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: A new paragraph begins, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅτι ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.

records.literal_gloss: He but answering said to them, Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, to those but not it has been given.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered and said to them, "Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to them it has not been given.
en.B: He answered them, "Because you have been allowed to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not.
en.R: Jesus answered, "God has let you know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven. These are secrets that God is now making known. But God has not let those other people know them.

es.L: Y respondiendo, les dijo: «Porque a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha dado conocer los misterios del reino de los cielos, pero a ellos no se les ha dado.
es.B: Él les respondió: «Porque a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha concedido conocer los misterios del reino de los cielos, pero a ellos no.
es.R: Jesús respondió: «Dios {{plural_you:les|os}} ha permitido a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} conocer los misterios del reino de los cielos. Son secretos que Dios ahora da a conocer. Pero a esa otra gente Dios no se lo ha permitido.

sw.L: Naye akajibu akawaambia, "Kwa sababu kwenu imetolewa kuzijua siri za ufalme wa mbinguni, lakini kwa wale haikutolewa.
sw.B: Akawajibu, "Kwa sababu ninyi mmejaliwa kuzifahamu siri za ufalme wa mbinguni, lakini wao hawakujaliwa.
sw.R: Yesu akajibu, "Mungu amewawezesha ninyi kuzijua siri za ufalme wa mbinguni. Hizi ni siri ambazo Mungu sasa anazifunua. Lakini wale watu wengine Mungu hajawawezesha kuzijua.

decisions.choice: mysteries: God's secrets, hidden until he makes them known
decisions.reason: In Daniel 2:28 God "reveals mysteries". The mysteries of the kingdom are what God is doing through Jesus. They are given, not worked out by cleverness (11:25-27).

decisions.choice: it has been given: God has given it
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the giver unnamed. In Jewish speech this often points to God, as in 11:25-27.

decisions.choice: because: Jesus gives the reason for speaking in parables
alternatives: introducing his words, like a colon
decisions.reason: The word can introduce quoted speech or give a reason. Here it answers the question "why".

decisions.choice: God has let you know; These are secrets that God is now making known
alternatives: it has been given to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the passive implies, keeps the word "mysteries" and says what it means.

decisions.choice: el reino de los cielos (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for Matthew, recorded once in this passage. The plural keeps Matthew's way of speaking of God's kingdom without naming God, as the Greek does.

decisions.choice: ufalme wa mbinguni (every level)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering for Matthew, recorded once in this passage. It keeps Matthew's way of speaking of God's kingdom without naming God.

decisions.choice: mmejaliwa ... hawakujaliwa (B)
decisions.reason: "Kujaliwa" is to be granted something by God, so Balanced says who gives (meaning decision m2) without adding a word; Literal keeps the impersonal passive and Readable names God, as the English Readable does.

source.text: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever for has, it will be given to him and he will have abundance; whoever but not has, even what he has will be taken away from him.

en.L: For whoever has, it will be given to {{gender:them|him}}, and {{gender:they|he}} will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what {{gender:they have|he has}} will be taken away from {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Those who have will be given more, and they will have plenty. But those who do not have will lose even what they have.
en.R: People who already have something will be given more. They will have more than enough. But people who have nothing will lose even the little they have.

es.L: Porque quien tiene, a él se le dará, y tendrá de sobra; pero quien no tiene, hasta lo que tiene se le quitará.
es.B: A los que tienen se les dará más, y tendrán de sobra. Pero a los que no tienen se les quitará hasta lo que tienen.
es.R: A las personas que ya tienen algo se les dará más. Tendrán más que suficiente. Pero a las que no tienen nada se les quitará incluso lo poco que tienen.

sw.L: Kwa maana yeyote aliye na kitu atapewa, naye atakuwa na zaidi ya kutosha; lakini yule asiye na kitu, hata kile anachokimiliki kitaondolewa kwake.
sw.B: Wale walio na kitu watapewa zaidi, nao watakuwa na vingi. Lakini wale wasio na kitu watapoteza hata kile walicho nacho.
sw.R: Watu ambao tayari wana kitu watapewa zaidi. Watakuwa na zaidi ya kutosha. Lakini watu wasio na kitu watapoteza hata kile kidogo walicho nacho.

decisions.choice: whoever has will be given more: those who accept what God gives will receive more understanding
alternatives: a saying about fairness in general
decisions.reason: The saying sounds like a proverb about wealth, but here it is about knowing the mysteries (13:11). The disciples have begun to understand and will be given more. Those who refuse lose even what they heard. Jesus uses the saying again in 25:29.

decisions.choice: will be given, will be taken away: God gives and takes
decisions.reason: As in 13:11, the passive points to God.

decisions.choice: those who (B); people who (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use plural forms, which include men and women.

decisions.choice: no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "him" as a traditional alternative. Spanish "quien" and "se le" already speak of anyone, so the setting has nothing to change, here or in verses 19-21.

decisions.choice: no gender spans
decisions.reason: The English Literal offers "him" as a traditional alternative, but "yeyote", "yule" and the verbs say nothing about sex, so the setting has nothing to change, here or in verses 19-21.

source.text: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν·

records.literal_gloss: Because of this in parables to them I speak, because seeing not they see and hearing not they hear nor understand;

en.L: This is why I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.
en.B: So I speak to them in parables, because they look without seeing and listen without hearing or understanding.
en.R: That is why I use parables when I talk to them. They look, but they do not really see. They listen, but they do not really hear or understand.

es.L: Por esto en parábolas les hablo: porque aunque ven, no ven, y aunque oyen, no oyen ni comprenden.
es.B: Por eso les hablo en parábolas: porque miran sin ver y escuchan sin oír ni entender.
es.R: Por eso uso parábolas cuando les hablo. Miran, pero en realidad no ven. Escuchan, pero en realidad no oyen ni entienden.

sw.L: Ndiyo maana kwa mifano ninaongea nao, kwa kuwa ingawa wanaona, hawaoni, na ingawa wanasikia, hawasikii wala hawafahamu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nasema nao kwa mifano, kwa sababu wanatazama bila kuona, na wanasikiliza bila kusikia wala kuelewa.
sw.R: Ndiyo sababu ninatumia mifano ninapozungumza nao. Wanatazama, lakini hawaoni kwa kweli. Wanasikiliza, lakini hawasikii kwa kweli, wala hawaelewi.

decisions.choice: because: they already do not see; the parables meet that state
alternatives: so that they will not see
decisions.reason: Mark 4:12 and Luke 8:10 say "so that", which stresses God's purpose. Matthew says "because", which stresses the hearers' own refusal. Both point to Isaiah 6:9-10, quoted next.

decisions.choice: seeing they do not see: they see the works and hear the words but miss what they mean
decisions.reason: The crowds have seen Jesus's works and heard his teaching (11:20-24; 12:22-24). They do not grasp what it shows.

decisions.choice: really see; really hear
decisions.reason: Readable adds "really" to show that the second seeing and hearing mean understanding.

source.text: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἠσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα· Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.

records.literal_gloss: And is fulfilled in them the prophecy of Isaiah the saying, In hearing you will hear and not not understand, and seeing you will see and not not perceive.

en.L: And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is being fulfilled, which says, 'You will hear with hearing and never understand, and you will see with seeing and never perceive.
en.B: In them the prophecy of Isaiah is coming true: 'You will listen and listen and never understand; you will look and look and never perceive.
en.R: They make the words of the prophet Isaiah come true. He said, 'You will listen and listen, but you will never understand. You will look and look, but you will never really see.

es.L: Y en ellos se está cumpliendo la profecía de Isaías, que dice: “Con el oído {{plural_you:oirán|oiréis}} y nunca {{plural_you:entenderán|entenderéis}}, y mirando {{plural_you:mirarán|miraréis}} y nunca {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}.
es.B: En ellos se está cumpliendo la profecía de Isaías: “{{plural_you:Escucharán|Escucharéis}} y {{plural_you:escucharán|escucharéis}}, pero nunca {{plural_you:entenderán|entenderéis}}; {{plural_you:mirarán|miraréis}} y {{plural_you:mirarán|miraréis}}, pero nunca {{plural_you:verán|veréis}}.
es.R: Así se cumple en ellos lo que dijo el profeta Isaías: “{{plural_you:Escucharán|Escucharéis}} y {{plural_you:escucharán|escucharéis}}, pero nunca {{plural_you:entenderán|entenderéis}}. {{plural_you:Mirarán|Miraréis}} y {{plural_you:mirarán|miraréis}}, pero nunca {{plural_you:verán|veréis}} de verdad.

sw.L: Na kwao unatimizwa unabii wa Isaya unaosema, 'Kwa masikio mtasikia, lakini hamtaelewa kamwe; na mkiona mtaona, lakini hamtatambua kamwe.
sw.B: Kwao unatimia unabii wa Isaya: 'Mtasikiliza na kusikiliza, lakini hamtaelewa kamwe; mtatazama na kutazama, lakini hamtatambua kamwe.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo maneno ya nabii Isaya yanatimia kwao. Alisema, 'Mtasikiliza na kusikiliza, lakini hamtaelewa kamwe. Mtatazama na kutazama, lakini hamtaona kamwe kwa kweli.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 6:9-10: God's word to Isaiah when he sent him to Israel
decisions.reason: God told Isaiah that the people would hear his message and not understand it. Matthew quotes the passage almost word for word from the Greek Old Testament. Paul uses the same words of his own hearers (Acts 28:26-27).

decisions.choice: is being fulfilled: is coming true in them now, in full
alternatives: was fulfilled once in Isaiah's day only
decisions.reason: The verb is present and has a strengthening prefix. What Isaiah's hearers did, this generation does again, and fully.

decisions.choice: you will hear with hearing, you will see with seeing: you will hear and see again and again
decisions.reason: The doubled verbs copy a Hebrew way of stressing an action.

decisions.choice: listen and listen, look and look
alternatives: hearing you will hear, seeing you will see
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb to show the force of the Hebrew idiom, as at Mark 4:12.

source.text: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μήποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.

records.literal_gloss: Has grown fat for the heart of the people this, and with the ears heavily they heard, and the eyes of them they closed; lest they see with the eyes and with the ears hear and with the heart understand and turn, and I will heal them.

en.L: For the heart of this people has grown fat, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and they have closed their eyes, lest they see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn, and I will heal them.'
en.B: This people's heart has grown dull. Their ears barely hear, and they have shut their eyes tight. If they did not, they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears, understand with their heart and turn back, and then I would heal them.'
en.R: These people have hearts that have become hard. Their ears hardly hear, and they have shut their eyes. Otherwise their eyes might see and their ears might hear. Their minds might understand, and they might turn back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. Then I would heal them.'

es.L: Porque el corazón de este pueblo se ha engordado, y con los oídos oyeron con dificultad, y cerraron sus ojos; no sea que con los ojos vean, y con los oídos oigan, y con el corazón comprendan, y se vuelvan, y yo los sanaré”.
es.B: El corazón de este pueblo se ha vuelto insensible. Apenas oyen con los oídos, y han cerrado bien los ojos. Si no fuera así, verían con los ojos y oirían con los oídos, entenderían con el corazón y se volverían, y yo los sanaría”.
es.R: El corazón de este pueblo se ha endurecido. Sus oídos casi no oyen, y han cerrado los ojos. Si no, sus ojos podrían ver y sus oídos podrían oír. Su mente podría entender, y podrían volverse a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Entonces yo los sanaría”.

sw.L: Kwa maana moyo wa watu hawa umenenepa, na kwa masikio yao wamesikia kwa uzito, na wameyafunga macho yao; isije ikawa waone kwa macho, na wasikie kwa masikio, na waelewe kwa moyo, na wageuke, nami nitawaponya.'
sw.B: Moyo wa watu hawa umepumbaa. Masikio yao hayasikii ila kwa shida, na macho yao wameyafunga kabisa. La sivyo, wangeona kwa macho yao na kusikia kwa masikio yao, wangeelewa kwa moyo wao na kurudi, nami ningewaponya.'
sw.R: Mioyo ya watu hawa imekuwa migumu. Masikio yao hayasikii vizuri, na wamefunga macho yao. Kama wasingefanya hivyo, macho yao yangeona na masikio yao yangesikia. Akili zao zingeelewa, nao wangenirudia {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. Kisha ningewaponya.'

decisions.choice: the heart has grown fat: the mind and will have become dull and unresponsive
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is where people think and choose. A fat heart is one that no longer feels or responds.

decisions.choice: lest ... and I will heal them: so that they will not turn and be healed
alternatives: in the hope that they might yet turn
decisions.reason: After "lest" the last verb is future, not subjunctive. It still belongs to what the people avoid: they shut their eyes so as not to turn and be healed. Some read the future as a hint of hope.

decisions.choice: turn: turn back to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the Old Testament word for returning to God, that is, repenting.

decisions.choice: heal: restore, forgive, make whole
decisions.reason: In Isaiah, healing pictures God's forgiveness and restoration of his people (Isaiah 53:5; 57:18-19).

decisions.choice: turn back to me
decisions.reason: Readable says who they would turn to. God is speaking, so "me" takes the deity_pronoun setting, as at 12:18.

decisions.choice: grown fat (L); grown dull (B); become hard (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of fat. Balanced and Readable say what it means.

source.text: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: Of you but blessed the eyes because they see, and the ears of you because they hear.

en.L: But blessed [are] your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
en.B: But your eyes are blessed, for they see, and so are your ears, for they hear.
en.R: But God has blessed you! Your eyes really see, and your ears really hear.

es.L: Pero de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, dichosos los ojos, porque ven, y los oídos {{plural_you:de ustedes|vuestros}}, porque oyen.
es.B: En cambio, dichosos {{plural_you:los ojos de ustedes|vuestros ojos}}, porque ven, y {{plural_you:los oídos de ustedes|vuestros oídos}}, porque oyen.
es.R: ¡Pero Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} ha bendecido a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}! {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestros}} ojos de verdad ven, y {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} oídos de verdad oyen.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi, heri [ni] macho yenu, kwa sababu yanaona, na masikio yenu, kwa sababu yanasikia.
sw.B: Lakini ninyi, macho yenu yamebarikiwa kwa sababu yanaona, na masikio yenu pia kwa sababu yanasikia.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu amewabariki ninyi! Macho yenu yanaona kwa kweli, na masikio yenu yanasikia kwa kweli.

decisions.choice: blessed: in the happy state of those God favors
decisions.reason: As in the Beatitudes (5:3-11). The disciples are favored because God has given them to see and hear (13:11).

decisions.choice: your: stressed, in contrast with the crowds
decisions.reason: The pronoun stands first in the Greek sentence: you, unlike them.

decisions.choice: God has blessed you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who blesses, and speaks of the disciples instead of their eyes and ears.

decisions.choice: dichosos (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in John 13:17 and 20:29: the word describes the happy state of those God favors (meaning decision m1). "Dichosos" says it in current Spanish; "bienaventurados" sounds churchly.

source.text: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.

records.literal_gloss: Truly for I say to you that many prophets and righteous longed to see what you see and not saw, and to hear what you hear and not heard.

en.L: For truly I tell you that many prophets and righteous [people] longed to see what you see, and did not see [it], and to hear what you hear, and did not hear [it].
en.B: Truly I tell you, many prophets and righteous people longed to see the things you now see, and never saw them; they longed to hear the things you now hear, and never heard them.
en.R: I tell you the truth, many prophets and righteous people wanted to see what you are seeing now. But they did not see it. They wanted to hear what you are hearing. But they did not hear it.

es.L: Porque en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que muchos profetas y justos anhelaron ver lo que {{plural_you:ustedes ven|vosotros veis}}, y no [lo] vieron, y escuchar lo que {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}, y no [lo] escucharon.
es.B: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que muchos profetas y muchos justos anhelaron ver las cosas que {{plural_you:ustedes ven|vosotros veis}} ahora, y nunca las vieron; anhelaron oír las cosas que ahora {{plural_you:oyen|oís}}, y nunca las oyeron.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: muchos profetas y muchas personas justas quisieron ver lo que {{plural_you:ustedes están|vosotros estáis}} viendo ahora. Pero no lo vieron. Quisieron oír lo que {{plural_you:están|estáis}} oyendo. Pero no lo oyeron.

sw.L: Kwa maana kweli nawaambia kwamba manabii wengi na [watu] wenye haki walitamani sana kuona mambo mnayoyaona, lakini hawakuyaona, na kusikia mambo mnayoyasikia, lakini hawakuyasikia.
sw.B: Kweli nawaambia, manabii wengi na watu wenye haki walitamani kuyaona mambo mnayoyaona sasa, lakini hawakuyaona; walitamani kuyasikia mambo mnayoyasikia sasa, lakini hawakuyasikia.
sw.R: Nawaambia ukweli: manabii wengi na watu wengi wenye haki walitaka kuona mambo mnayoyaona sasa. Lakini hawakuyaona. Walitaka kusikia mambo mnayoyasikia. Lakini hawakuyasikia.

decisions.choice: prophets and righteous people: the faithful of Israel before Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls those who waited for God's promises (10:41; 23:29). They looked forward to the time of the kingdom.

decisions.choice: what you see and hear: the coming of God's kingdom in Jesus
decisions.reason: The disciples see Jesus's works and hear his words, which fulfill what the prophets hoped for (11:4-6).

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The settled wording of Jesus's solemn saying.

decisions.choice: En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo (L, B); {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of Jesus's single "amen" for the Gospels, recorded once in this passage; John's doubled form is "En verdad, en verdad".

decisions.choice: Kweli nawaambia (L, B); Nawaambia ukweli (R)
decisions.reason: The term-sheet rendering of Jesus's single "amen" for the Gospels, recorded once in this passage; "Kweli kweli nawaambia" stays for John's doubled form.

source.text: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.

records.literal_gloss: You therefore hear the parable of the having sown.

en.L: You, therefore, hear the parable of the sower.
en.B: As for you, then, hear what the parable of the sower means.
en.R: So listen, and I will explain to you the parable about the farmer.

es.L: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, pues, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} la parábola del que sembró.
es.B: En cuanto a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}} lo que significa la parábola del sembrador.
es.R: Así que {{plural_you:escuchen|escuchad}}, y {{plural_you:les|os}} explicaré la parábola del agricultor.

sw.L: Ninyi basi, usikieni mfano wa yule aliyepanda.
sw.B: Basi ninyi, sikilizeni maana ya mfano wa mpandaji.
sw.R: Basi sikilizeni, nitawaeleza maana ya mfano wa yule mkulima.

decisions.choice: you: stressed, the disciples to whom it has been given to know
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out for emphasis, as in 13:16.

decisions.choice: hear: listen with understanding
decisions.reason: The disciples have already heard the story. Jesus now gives its meaning.

decisions.choice: hear what the parable means (B); I will explain (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the explanation follows.

source.text: παντὸς ἀκούοντος τὸν λόγον τῆς βασιλείας καὶ μὴ συνιέντος, ἔρχεται ὁ πονηρὸς καὶ ἁρπάζει τὸ ἐσπαρμένον ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ αὐτοῦ· οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν σπαρείς.

records.literal_gloss: Everyone hearing the word of the kingdom and not understanding, comes the evil one and snatches the having been sown in the heart of him; this is the beside the road having been sown.

en.L: When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand [it], the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in {{gender:their|his}} heart; this is what was sown beside the road.
en.B: Here is the seed sown beside the path: people who hear the message of the kingdom without understanding it. The evil one comes and carries off what was sown in their hearts.
en.R: Some people hear the message about God's kingdom, but they do not understand it. They are like the seed that fell on the path. The evil one, Satan, comes and takes away what was planted in their hearts.

es.L: Todo el que oye la palabra del reino y no [la] comprende: viene el maligno y arrebata lo que se sembró en su corazón; este es el sembrado junto al camino.
es.B: La semilla sembrada al borde del sendero es como quien oye el mensaje del reino sin entenderlo: viene el maligno y se lleva lo que se sembró en su corazón.
es.R: Algunas personas oyen el mensaje sobre el reino de Dios, pero no lo entienden. Son como la semilla que cayó en el camino. El maligno, Satanás, viene y les quita lo que se sembró en su corazón.

sw.L: Kila mtu anayelisikia neno la ufalme bila kulielewa, anakuja yule mwovu na kukinyakua kilichopandwa ndani ya moyo wake; huyu ni yule aliyepandwa kando ya njia.
sw.B: Mbegu iliyopandwa kando ya njia ni mtu anayesikia ujumbe wa ufalme bila kuuelewa. Yule mwovu anakuja na kukinyakua kile kilichopandwa moyoni mwake.
sw.R: Watu wengine husikia ujumbe kuhusu ufalme wa Mungu, lakini hawauelewi. Wao ni kama mbegu zilizoanguka njiani. Yule mwovu, Shetani, anakuja na kuchukua kile kilichopandwa mioyoni mwao.

decisions.choice: the evil one: the devil
decisions.reason: Here the form is clearly masculine: the evil one comes and snatches. In 13:39 the enemy is the devil; compare 5:37 and 6:13.

decisions.choice: the word of the kingdom: the message that God's kingdom has come near
decisions.reason: Jesus preached the gospel of the kingdom (4:17, 23). The seed is that message.

decisions.choice: this is what was sown beside the road: the hearer is compared with the seed sown there
decisions.reason: Jesus's words shift between the seed and the ground. The point is what happens to the word in each kind of hearer.

decisions.choice: the evil one, Satan
decisions.reason: Readable says who the evil one is, as 13:39 does ("the devil").

decisions.choice: the identification first: Here is the seed sown beside the path
decisions.reason: Balanced names the kind of ground first so that the long sentence is easy to follow when read aloud.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνων αὐτόν, οὐκ ἔχει δὲ ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτῷ ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιρός ἐστιν, γενομένης δὲ θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζεται.

records.literal_gloss: The but upon the rocky places having been sown, this is the one the word hearing and immediately with joy receiving it, \v 21 not he has but root in himself but temporary is, having happened but tribulation or persecution because of the word immediately he is caused to stumble.

en.L: And what was sown on the rocky places, this is the one who hears the word and at once receives it with joy, \v 21 but has no root in {{gender:themselves|himself}} and lasts only for a time; and when trouble or persecution comes because of the word, at once {{gender:they fall|he falls}} away.
en.B: The seed sown on the rocky ground is the person who hears the word and at once accepts it with joy. \v 21 But the word has no root in them, and they hold on only for a while. As soon as hardship or persecution comes on account of the word, they stumble and fall away.
en.R: Other people are like the rocky ground. They hear the message and right away they accept it with joy. \v 21 But they do not let it put down roots in them, so they last only a short time. Then trouble comes, or people hurt them because of the message. Right away they give up.

es.L: Y el sembrado sobre los terrenos pedregosos, ese es el que oye la palabra y enseguida la acepta con alegría; \v 21 pero no tiene raíz en sí mismo, sino que es pasajero, y al llegar una tribulación o persecución a causa de la palabra, enseguida se aparta.
es.B: Lo sembrado en terreno pedregoso es quien oye la palabra y enseguida la acepta con alegría. \v 21 Pero la palabra no echa raíz en su interior, y se mantiene firme solo por un tiempo. En cuanto llegan las dificultades o la persecución por causa de la palabra, tropieza y se aparta.
es.R: Otras personas son como el terreno lleno de piedras. Oyen el mensaje y enseguida lo aceptan con alegría. \v 21 Pero no dejan que eche raíces en ellas, y por eso duran poco tiempo. Luego vienen los problemas, o la gente las maltrata por causa del mensaje. Y enseguida abandonan.

sw.L: Na yule aliyepandwa kwenye sehemu zenye miamba, huyu ndiye anayelisikia neno na mara moja analipokea kwa furaha, \v 21 lakini hana mzizi ndani yake mwenyewe, bali ni wa kitambo tu; na inapotokea taabu au mateso kwa sababu ya neno, mara moja anajikwaa.
sw.B: Mbegu iliyopandwa kwenye sehemu yenye miamba ni mtu anayesikia neno na mara moja kulipokea kwa furaha. \v 21 Lakini neno halitii mizizi ndani yake, naye hushikilia kwa muda mfupi tu. Mara tu taabu au mateso yanapokuja kwa sababu ya neno, anajikwaa na kuanguka.
sw.R: Watu wengine ni kama ardhi yenye mawe. Wanasikia ujumbe, na mara moja wanaupokea kwa furaha. \v 21 Lakini hawauruhusu ujumbe kutia mizizi ndani yao, kwa hiyo wanadumu muda mfupi tu. Kisha taabu zinakuja, au watu wanawatesa kwa sababu ya ujumbe huo. Mara moja wanaacha kuufuata.

decisions.choice: falls away: is tripped up and stops following
decisions.reason: The verb means to trip over something. Here the trouble makes them give up the word they received.

decisions.choice: lasts only for a time: temporary, not lasting
decisions.reason: The word means "for a season". Their joy is real but does not last.

decisions.choice: trouble or persecution: hardship, and attacks from others
decisions.reason: The first word means pressure or distress, the second being hunted down for one's faith (5:10-12).

decisions.choice: give up
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for what the verb means here.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων, καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος τούτου καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.

records.literal_gloss: The but into the thorns having been sown, this is the one the word hearing, and the worry of the age this and the deceit of the riches choke the word, and unfruitful it becomes.

en.L: And what was sown among the thorns, this is the one who hears the word, and the worry of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
en.B: The seed sown among the thorns is the person who hears the word, but the cares of the present age and the false promises of wealth smother it, so that it yields no crop.
en.R: Other people are like the ground with thorny weeds. They hear the message, but then they worry about the things of this life. They are fooled into thinking that being rich will make them happy. These things crowd out the message, so it does not produce anything in their lives.

es.L: Y el sembrado entre las espinas, ese es el que oye la palabra, y la inquietud de esta era y lo engañoso de la riqueza sofocan la palabra, y queda sin fruto.
es.B: Lo sembrado entre las zarzas es quien oye la palabra, pero las preocupaciones de esta vida presente y las falsas promesas de la riqueza la sofocan, y no da cosecha.
es.R: Otras personas son como el terreno con hierbas espinosas. Oyen el mensaje, pero después viven preocupadas por las cosas de esta vida. Se dejan engañar y creen que la riqueza las hará felices. Estas cosas ahogan el mensaje, y por eso no produce nada en su vida.

sw.L: Na yule aliyepandwa kati ya miiba, huyu ndiye anayelisikia neno, na wasiwasi wa zama hizi na hila ya utajiri vinalikaba neno, nalo linakuwa bila matunda.
sw.B: Mbegu iliyopandwa kati ya miiba ni mtu anayesikia neno, lakini masumbufu ya maisha ya sasa na ahadi za uongo za utajiri hulikaba neno hilo, nalo halitoi mavuno.
sw.R: Watu wengine ni kama ardhi yenye magugu ya miiba. Wanasikia ujumbe, lakini kisha wanahangaika na mambo ya maisha haya. Wanadanganyika wakidhani kwamba kuwa matajiri kutawafanya wawe na furaha. Mambo hayo yanaubana ujumbe, kwa hiyo hauzai chochote katika maisha yao.

decisions.choice: the worry of this age: the anxious cares of life in the present world
alternatives: concern for the end of the world
decisions.reason: Jesus warned against such worry in 6:25-34. "This age" is the present time, before the age to come (12:32).

decisions.choice: the deceitfulness of wealth: riches that promise what they cannot give
decisions.reason: The word means deceit or seduction. Wealth draws the heart away from God (6:19-24; 19:21-24).

decisions.choice: it becomes unfruitful: the word produces no crop in that person
decisions.reason: The plant does not die at once. It grows but gives no grain.

decisions.choice: They are fooled into thinking that being rich will make them happy
decisions.reason: Readable explains how wealth deceives.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.

records.literal_gloss: The but upon the good soil having been sown, this is the one the word hearing and understanding, who indeed bears fruit and produces, some indeed a hundred, some but sixty, some but thirty.

en.L: But what was sown on the good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands [it], who indeed bears fruit and produces, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty."
en.B: But the seed sown on good soil is the person who hears the word and understands it. That person does bear fruit, yielding a hundred times what was sown, or sixty, or thirty."
en.R: But some people are like the good soil. They hear the message and understand it. Then they produce a good crop. Some produce a hundred times as much as was planted, some sixty times as much, and some thirty times as much."

es.L: Y el sembrado sobre la tierra buena, ese es el que oye la palabra y [la] entiende, el que sí da fruto y produce: uno cien [veces], otro sesenta, otro treinta».
es.B: Pero lo sembrado en buena tierra es quien oye la palabra y la entiende. Esa persona sí da fruto, y produce cien veces más de lo sembrado, o sesenta, o treinta».
es.R: Pero otras personas son como la tierra buena. Oyen el mensaje y lo entienden. Entonces producen una buena cosecha. Algunas producen cien veces más de lo que se sembró, otras sesenta veces más y otras treinta veces más».

sw.L: Lakini yule aliyepandwa juu ya ardhi nzuri, huyu ndiye anayelisikia neno na kulielewa, ndiye hasa anayezaa matunda na kuyatoa, mmoja [mara] mia, mwingine sitini, mwingine thelathini."
sw.B: Lakini mbegu iliyopandwa kwenye udongo mzuri ni mtu anayesikia neno na kulielewa. Mtu huyo kweli hutoa mazao, mara mia ya kile kilichopandwa, au mara sitini, au mara thelathini."
sw.R: Lakini watu wengine ni kama udongo mzuri. Wanasikia ujumbe na kuuelewa. Kisha wanatoa mavuno mazuri. Wengine wanatoa mavuno mara mia ya kile kilichopandwa, wengine mara sitini, na wengine mara thelathini."

decisions.choice: hears and understands: takes in the message and grasps it
decisions.reason: Understanding is the difference between this hearer and the first (13:19). It is what the crowds lack (13:13-15).

decisions.choice: bears fruit: shows the word in a changed life
decisions.reason: Fruit in Matthew means the deeds that show what a person is (3:8; 7:16-20; 12:33).

decisions.choice: who indeed: this one, and no other, bears fruit
decisions.reason: The small word adds emphasis.
